t: Richard Mentor Johnson became the only person ever to be elected Vice President of the United States by the Senate.
Chicago was incorporated as a city.
A fire broke out in Surat, India, which went on to destroy about 75% of the city.
Tensions between Yankees and Irish Americans in Boston, Massachusetts, erupted in the Broad Street Riot.
Queen Victoria acceded to the British throne, beginning a 63-year reign.
The Grand Junction Railway, the world's first long-distance railway with steam traction, opened between Birmingham and Newton Junction.
Daaga and two other African soldiers in the British Army's 1st West India Regiment were executed for their role in the St. Joseph Mutiny in Trinidad.
American abolitionist Elijah Parish Lovejoy was murdered by a pro-slavery mob in Alton, Illinois, during an attack to destroy his printing press and abolitionist materials.
British troops swiftly defeated rebels led by William Lyon Mackenzie and Anthony Van Egmond at the Battle of Montgomery's Tavern, the only major confrontation of the Upper Canada Rebellion.
